### jointAngles {#jointangles}

How far each joint of a finger bends in a closed fist, in degrees, from the metacarpal out.

Angles rather than a search, because this is the one thing about a hand that does not
depend on how big the hand is. A fist is a fist at any scale: the metacarpals barely move,
the knuckle folds to a right angle, the joint past it slightly further, and the last one
less. Searching for where the fingertip meets the palm instead sounds more general and is
not - it stops wherever the tip happens to pass nearest, which on a real hand is halfway
through the curl, leaving a cupped hand rather than a closed one.

A chain longer than this list repeats the last angle; a shorter one uses what it needs.

```csharp

```

### palmClearance {#palmclearance}

How far a fingertip may pass back out through the palm before the curl is cut short, in metres.

A safety net for a rig the angles above do not suit - a short finger on a broad hand - and
nothing else. On a hand they do suit it never comes into play.


### thumbAngles {#thumbangles}

The same for the thumb, which bends far less and about a different axis.

A thumb opposes rather than folds: its base is a saddle joint, it swings across the palm
instead of onto it, and bending it like a finger curls it into the hand rather than over
whatever the hand is holding.
